title: Uma Shankar v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Saumitra Dayal Singh and Indrajeet Shukla, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; Assessing Officer to decide objection under clause 6.8 after hearing.
headnote: Where electricity assessment was concluded ex parte, the writ was disposed by relegating the consumer to Clause 6.8: on deposit of Rs. 1,75,000 and filing of an objection, the Assessing Officer must decide by a reasoned order after confronting the consumer with adverse material and granting personal hearing; non-compliance revives the recovery.
facts: The petitioner challenged a recovery citation dated 26 June 2025 seeking Rs. 7,26,244 towards electricity dues. Counsel for the distribution licensee, on written instructions retained on record, disclosed that both provisional and final assessments had been made on 11 November 2024 for that sum. Those pleadings and instructions showed that the entire assessment had been conducted and concluded ex parte against the petitioner.

holding_units.topic: ex-parte assessment — hearing before Assessing Officer
holding_units.holding: Where provisional and final assessment of electricity dues were conducted and concluded ex parte, no useful purpose is served by keeping the writ pending. Subject to the consumer depositing Rs. 1,75,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and filing an application within a further week, the Assessing Officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order under Clause 6.8, after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months; non-compliance revives the recovery from that stage.

not_decided.point: Merits of the assessment and recovery citation of Rs. 7,26,244
not_decided.note: Left to the Assessing Officer under clause 6.8.
